rulings.decision: Proposal A, with the spans worded here. The claim is contradicted by the bytes of both witnesses and is corrected in FIXUP-4, W1 only, one lane. In W1-002.boundary_rationale the author makes exactly two changes: (1) the replacement 'the steward's fear -> the fear of the prince of the eunuchs'; (2) the insertion 'vegetables (1:16). -> vegetables (1:16) (INFERRED).'. The clause 'ending when the steward keeps giving vegetables (1:16)' is NOT contradicted and is left as written.
rulings.reason: EXTRACTED by me from both pinned witnesses (script work\r1.py printed the verses; I read them). Dan_web_clean.txt 1:10 opens 'The prince of the eunuchs said to Daniel' and holds 'I fear my lord the king'; 1:11 first names 'the steward whom the prince of the eunuchs had appointed'. Dan_oshb.txt Dan.1.10 has the speaker as words 2-3 (sar ha-sarisim) and the fear as words 5-6 (yare ani); Dan.1.11 names ha-meltsar as the one whom that prince appointed. So the fear belongs to the prince of the eunuchs and the steward is a second official: the row's words are wrong in both witnesses, and this is not a divided reading. MEASURED (work\r1.py, work\r2.py): 'the steward's fear' occurs once in the field and once in the whole rows file; 'vegetables (1:16).' occurs once in the field; the after-phrase is absent before. Why correct now and not send it on: a claim already measured false would cost both blind primaries a finding each on a known defect, and a row that names the wrong speaker is a false statement about the text (OW-18). The correction only makes the row say what the bytes say: 'prince of the eunuchs' is the witness's own title at 1:10; no reading is added. Why (INFERRED) and not EXTRACTED: the sentence is a summary that mixes witness facts with the author's outline of the episode, and 'keeps giving' is a reading of aspect: Dan_web_clean.txt 1:16 has the simple past ('took away ... and gave them vegetables'), while Dan_oshb.txt Dan.1.16 has vayehi with two participles (nose, noten), which supports a continuing practice but is a grammatical inference, not a quotation. An order may not raise a tier above the bytes; INFERRED is the tier that is true of the whole sentence, and it is how the FIXUP-3 authors tiered mixed sentences. On the last clause: the subject at 1:16 is the steward in both witnesses, so that clause stands. The new span holds no digit, no file stem and no format token, so it cannot add a CWO-DAN-01..04 hit (predicates read from E1); the orchestrator still measures that (F7). No ruling here adjudicates a divided reading, a textual reading or a timeline.

(a) W4-011 'the seer seeks understanding (EXTRACTED, WEB)': Dan_web_clean.txt 8:15 has 'I sought to understand it' (and Dan_oshb.txt Dan.8.15 va-avaqsha vina); the claim is in the named layer's bytes, in paraphrase with the tense changed. The tier is true; no change. (b) W4-011 'where Gabriel comes near (8:17) (INFERRED)': Dan_web_clean.txt 8:17 has 'So he came near where I stood' and the name stands only in 8:16, in the voice's address; that 'he' is Gabriel is a reading. INFERRED is right; no change. (c) A sentence that mixes a witness fact with a reading and is tiered INFERRED states less than it could and nothing false; strategy section 8 item 7 forbids a stronger word, not a weaker one. No change; I used the same tier for W1-002. (d) W2-007 strongest_rejected_alternative first sentence ('Fold 3:30 back into 3:28-30 with the blessing and decree.') states the rival; it is a proposal, not a fact about a witness and not a conclusion, the field holds an annotation, and opening W2 for it would add a lane for no claim. No change. W1-010 last sentence ('Region (o), a weak edge, for the end review.') is different: 'a weak edge' is a conclusion of the kind E3 rule (c) names ('a seam is weak'), not a bare pointer, though the strategy lists region (o) among its expected low-confidence regions (book_strategy_Dan.md line 346). W1 is open anyway, the span is unique (MEASURED, work\r2.py: count 1) and INFERRED is true of a weighing. Ordered. (e) W1's seven device_notes of the form 'Aramaic narrative (MEASURED, language-zone layer)' (W1-007..W1-013, and 'wholly in the Aramaic section' in W1-006; MEASURED list, work\r1.py): the layer named is a language layer, so the MEASURED word is true of the language word only; the genre word beside it (narrative, hymn, dialogue, report) is the row's reading and is NOT measured. I say this in words because a reader may take the annotation to cover both (OW-18). I do not order a change: the grammar G offers no way to tier one word of a two-word phrase without adding words, which the TIER-ONLY RULE forbids, and the language-zone file is not among my inputs, so I could not check the claim I would be re-tiering. It goes to the primaries and the end review as a named weakness.
